variable_pay.title: Payroll 5 — Variable Pay: Overtime, Bonuses, Commissions & Deductions
variable_pay.desc: The one-offs' governed home: the additional-salary machinery, overtime through one channel with the price-signal read, bonuses as documents with the policy-versus-gift line, commissions computed from selling documents with statements and clawback clauses, arrears travelling forward with shown arithmetic, staff lending mechanics with the welfare read, and off-cycle payments as mini-runs.

lessons.title: Chapter 1 — Variable pay: governed, not improvised
lessons.html:
The structure computes the same numbers every month — and every month, real life adds to them: the overtime worked, the bonus earned, the commission closed, the correction owed, the loan advancing. This module governs the layer where those one-offs live: variable pay — and its thesis is the line this track has drawn since module 1: variable pay is governed, not improvised.

Why this layer is where structure leaks. The diagnosis first, because the consultant will meet it everywhere: the FIXED pay is easy to govern (the structure holds it; the review changes it; nobody types it) — but the variable layer is where every governance instinct meets its temptation: the bonus is discretionary (so why paper it?), the overtime is small (so why gate it?), the correction is urgent (so why wait?), the advance is a kindness (so why policy it?) — and the trade's payrolls answer those four questions wrongly for years until the layer is a parallel economy: cash envelopes beside the bank run, commissions computed from a salesperson's own notebook, corrections negotiated at the counter, and lending that is really the founder's personal favour book. The cost is every disease this academy has named at once — the favour system (unevenness denominated in naira), the version drift (the slip that doesn't know about the envelope), the tax leak (the cash bonus module 2's projection never saw), and the fraud surface (the variable layer is where the padding, the phantom overtime, and the invented one-off live, because it is the layer where numbers are typed).

The cure: the additional-salary machinery. One instrument governs the whole layer: every variable item is a DOCUMENT — the additional-pay entry carrying its TYPE (the component it posts to — module 1's variable components receiving their population), its AMOUNT (or the computation that produces it — Chapters 2 and 4's derived items), its AUTHORITY (who approved, per the type's approval rule — the spot bonus's approver is named policy, not ambient generosity), its PERIOD (the run that will carry it — the cutoff of module 3 governing admission), and its REFERENCE (the source it derives from — the overtime sheet, the scheme, the arrears computation, the instrument). The document then flows the run's ritual like everything else: validated (module 3's pending-document read), computed (onto the slip as its labelled line — module 4's anatomy), posted (to its component's ledger address), and archived (the variable layer's history as readable as the fixed layer's — which is the whole point: the one-off that is a document is one-off in AMOUNT but standard in GOVERNANCE).

The module's map. The variable earnings first — overtime (Chapter 2), bonuses (Chapter 3), commissions (Chapter 4 — the Selling track's crossover); the corrections layer — arrears and adjustments travelling forward (Chapter 5 — module 3's frozen-run law cashing its promise); the lending layer — loans and advances at mechanics depth (Chapter 6 — module 4's consent layer receiving its machinery); and the off-cycle payments that leave the monthly ritual without leaving governance (Chapter 7). One case study, one pattern set, one law — and the thread throughout: the variable layer run as documents is the difference between a payroll that flexes and a payroll that leaks.

lessons.title: Chapter 2 — Overtime: hours into money, one channel
lessons.html:
The commonest variable earning, and the one whose governance the run already settled — this chapter completes it: the policy, the channel, the approval, and the read. The overtime chapter.

The policy first. Overtime exists as a POLICY before it exists as a payment: WHO is eligible (role-based — the operational roles whose extra hours are compensable, distinguished from the salaried-inclusive roles whose contracts absorb reasonable extension: the line the adviser confirms and the contracts state, because the eligibility argued case-by-case is the fairness leak at its most frequent), the RATE (the multiplier convention — the policy stating its multiple of the derived hourly rate, with the hourly rate COMPUTED from the structure: the monthly-salary-to-hourly derivation stated once — the divisor convention explicit — so every overtime naira traces to the structure like everything else), the CAPS and authorisations (the monthly overtime ceiling per person that flags the roster problem before it becomes a budget problem — Chapter's read below), and the WEEKEND/holiday treatments where policy differentiates them (stated, not remembered).

The one channel. Module 3's case-law rule, now with its full reasoning: overtime enters payroll through the ATTENDANCE PACKAGE only — the hours captured by the HR track's machinery (the check-ins that bound the shift, the overtime approved against the captured hours), closed in the attendance close, and delivered in the monthly cargo — never through a side list, a supervisor's text, or a direct additional-pay entry (the double-counting HealthTrade met in module 3 was exactly two channels carrying one truth; the fix was the channel count, not the vigilance). The discipline's dividend: overtime hours are FACTS from the capture layer (disputed hours resolved by the check-in trail, not by recollection), and the padding fraud's surface shrinks to the approval step — which is why the approval is designed next.

Approval: before the hours, not after the fact. The governance's timing rule: overtime is APPROVED IN ADVANCE as the norm (the supervisor authorising the extension before it is worked — the roster's coverage decision made consciously, with the cost visible), with the discovered-overtime path as the governed exception (the emergency extension worked first and regularised within the window — module 3 of the HR track's regularisation discipline applying, bounded and reasoned), because after-the-fact overtime as the NORM is unmanaged cost plus unmanageable verification (the hours already worked can only be disputed, never declined — the approval that can only say yes is not an approval), and the approver's economics are taught plainly: the overtime hour costs its multiple; the roster fix costs a conversation — Chapter's read makes the comparison monthly.

The overtime read. The layer's altitude discipline, closing the chapter: overtime read monthly at the pattern level — the CHRONIC overtime (the same role, every month, is not a surge; it is a staffing gap wearing a premium rate — the HR track's headcount conversation triggered by payroll's number: the trilogy's reads meshing), the CLUSTERED overtime (one supervisor's team consistently authorising heavy hours is a management read — the padding question asked politely by the data: the hours against the capture trail, the approvals against the pattern, module 3's session-variance epistemics applied to hours), the SEASONAL overtime (the festive-season surge that is real, planned, and budgeted — the calendar's known shape, distinguished from drift), and the ZERO overtime in roles that plainly extend (the unrecorded extension is either goodwill burning out or hours moving through a side channel — both worth finding). The read's one-line summary for the owner's page: overtime is a price signal — it prices the roster's gaps, and the firm that reads it staffs deliberately while the firm that doesn't pays time-and-a-half for its planning debt.

lessons.title: Chapter 3 — Bonuses: the discretionary layer, governed
lessons.html:
The variable earning with the widest discretion and therefore the strongest need for governance: the bonus — kept generous AND governed, because the two are not opposites. The bonus chapter.

The bonus taxonomy. The types, each with its governance shape: the performance bonus (fed by the HR track's appraisal machinery — the rating-linked payout where policy runs one, computed from the calibrated outcome per the published rule: the bonus that traces to the folder is an incentive; the one that traces to a mood is a lottery, and the workforce knows which it is playing within two cycles), the festive/thirteenth-month payment (where the firm runs one — a POLICY, stated in the terms, scheduled as Chapter 7's second run, and budgeted from January, because the thirteenth month discovered in November is a cashflow ambush the firm aimed at itself), the spot bonus (the immediate recognition — the generator sorted, the save at the counter — governed lightest but governed: the named approvers, the per-instance cap, the document with its reason: HealthTrade's ₦30k in module 1 was exactly this machinery, thirty seconds of process), and the scheme payouts beyond (the target bonuses, the retention payments — each per its written rule).

Every bonus a document. The machinery applied: the bonus as an additional-pay entry with its type, authority, and reason — landing on the slip as its LABELLED line (module 4's anatomy: the bonus the worker can see and name is recognition twice — once in naira, once in respect; the mystery credit is recognition wasted), posted to its component's address (the bonus expense visible in the cost-center P&L — Accounts 6 seeing what generosity costs where), and TAXED correctly (the bonus is taxable income — module 2's annual projection absorbing it in its month, the PAYE spike explained by the frame the payroll seat can narrate: the bonus month's tax question is Chapter 5 of module 4's catalogued query, pre-answered by the announcement that accompanies the payout). The cash-envelope alternative convicted with its full bill: the off-book bonus is a tax exposure (the income module 2's computation never saw), an evenness breach (the envelope has no policy), a ledger hole (the cash that left without an address), and a precedent (the envelope's recipient learned where generosity lives — outside the system, which is where they will look for it next time).

Policy versus gift. The chapter's governing distinction, drawn once and used forever: the bonus that is POLICY (the thirteenth month, the scheme payout, the rating-linked amount) is an ENTITLEMENT once its conditions are met — administered evenly, computed from its rule, disputed against its rule (the HR track's entitlement law reaching the discretionary layer: what the policy grants, the mood cannot withhold) — while the bonus that is GIFT (the spot recognition, the discretionary year-end) is discretion EXERCISED within governance (the named approver, the cap, the document — discretion about WHO and HOW MUCH, never about whether the machinery applies). The confusion of the two is the layer's classic wound in both directions: the 'discretionary' thirteenth month withheld in a tight year from staff whose contracts state it (an entitlement breached, with the adviser about to be involved), and the spot bonus institutionalised by repetition until its absence is a grievance (the gift that hardened into an expectation nobody priced — the consultant's advice: the recurring gift should either become policy deliberately or vary visibly, because the third path, the accidental entitlement, is chosen by default and paid for annually).

lessons.title: Chapter 4 — Commissions: the selling crossover
lessons.html:
The variable earning that joins two certifications: the commission — earned at the counter the Selling track governs, paid through the run this track governs, and computed from DOCUMENTS at both ends. The crossover chapter.

The scheme is written. The commission exists as a SCHEME before anyone sells: the written rule stating the BASE (commission on WHAT — the invoiced sale, the collected payment, the margin: the base decision is the scheme's whole character, and the Selling track taught its consequences — the invoice-based scheme pays for sales; the collection-based scheme pays for MONEY, and the trade's receivables discipline usually argues for the latter or a split), the RATE structure (flat, tiered, threshold-gated — per the written table), the PERIOD (the month or quarter it computes over), the ELIGIBILITY (the roles in the scheme, the joiner's proration, the leaver's treatment — Chapter's clause below), and the CAPS and gates where the design uses them (the target gate, the ceiling). The scheme signed and filed like the structure it is — because the commission dispute without a written scheme is two recollections negotiating, and the salesperson's version is always, honestly, larger.

Computed from source documents. The discipline that makes commission a computation instead of a negotiation: the commission derives from the SELLING TRACK'S DOCUMENTS — the invoices, the collections, the credit notes — pulled by the scheme's rule over the period (the sales register's numbers, not the salesperson's notebook and not the manager's memory: the two tracks' machinery joining at the computation, which is why the consultant who holds both certifications configures this in an hour while the single-track consultant mediates it forever), the computation GENERATED as the additional-pay document with its reference (the period's source list attached — the commission's provenance as walkable as the slip's), and the anti-pattern named for every cleanup engagement: commission-from-memory (the month-end negotiation over a notebook) is the variable layer's version-drift disease at its most contentious, because it monthly re-litigates the firm's biggest incentive.

The clawback clause. The scheme's hard edge, designed in daylight: the commission paid on the sale that REVERSES (the returned goods, the cancelled invoice, the collection that bounces) — governed by the scheme's own clause (the reversal netting against the period's computation, or the clawback recovering per the stated rule — decided at design, stated in the scheme, consented per module 4's layer), because the clawback IMPROVISED at the first big return is a grievance with a calculator (the salesperson who was never told the rule experiences the recovery as confiscation — module 4's never-surprised law applying to the downside exactly as to the upside), and the netting mechanics kept honest (the reversal visible in the commission statement's lines, not silently shrinking a total).

The commission statement. The layer's transparency instrument, closing the chapter: each period's commission accompanied by its STATEMENT — the source documents listed (the invoices/collections in the base), the rule applied visibly (the tier reached, the gate passed), the reversals netted with their references, and the payout reconciling to the slip's line — the salesperson's own reconciliation document (module 4's answered-by-pointing, pre-delivered: the seller who can audit their own commission does, monthly, for free — twenty-seven personal auditors' logic at the incentive layer), and the statement's quiet second service: the commission data read at altitude joins the Selling track's scheme reads (the scheme that pays out against flat sales has a base problem; the seller earning far off the pack's curve is either the star the firm should study or the anomaly the firm should audit — both worth knowing, neither visible without the statement's data). The crossover's summary, for the certification's sales pitch: commission done this way costs one configuration and zero monthly arguments — and the firm's biggest incentive finally points exactly where the scheme aimed it.

lessons.title: Chapter 5 — Arrears & adjustments: corrections travel forward
lessons.html:
Module 3 froze the run and promised the corrections a home; this chapter is the home: the arrears and adjustments layer — where errors are corrected honestly, visibly, and FORWARD. The corrections chapter.

The underpayment: arrears. The correction owed TO the worker (the missed increment, the dropped overtime hour, the validation miss surfacing late): governed as a document — the ARREARS entry carrying its computation SHOWN (the difference derived: what should have computed, what did, the delta per period — module 1's walk applied to the gap, because the arrears figure asserted without its arithmetic is a new dispute wearing a correction), its periods identified (which sealed months it repairs — referenced, never reopened: the frozen runs stand; the repair lands in the current run as its labelled line), its authority (the correction approved like any variable item), and its COMMUNICATION (module 4's law: the arrears announced to its recipient with the honest account — we found it, here is the arithmetic, here is when it lands — the error converted into the trust deposit module 4 described). The tax note carried with it: the arrears is income in its payment month (module 2's projection absorbing it — the spike explained in the announcement, pre-empting the query).

The backdated change: computed, not estimated. The commonest arrears species, given its machinery: the increment or promotion effective in a PAST month (the review that concluded late, the movement processed after its date — HR 7's effective dates meeting module 3's cutoffs): the system computes the backdated difference PER PERIOD from the assignment's effective date (the months between the effective date and the processing date each re-derived against the new structure — the machinery's arithmetic, not a lump-sum estimate), lands it as the arrears line with its breakdown, and the discipline's contrast is the cleanup engagement's daily find: the backdated raise 'settled' with a round number nobody can derive — generous or short, nobody knows, and the not-knowing is the injury.

The overpayment: the recovery conversation. The correction owed BY the worker — the harder direction, governed accordingly: the overpayment established with its arithmetic (the same shown computation, both directions honest), the CONVERSATION before the deduction (module 4's never-surprised law at its most necessary — the recovery discovered on a slip is an ambush with the firm's error as its author: the person told, the arithmetic walked, the recovery agreed), the recovery CONSENTED and SCHEDULED (module 4's instrument layer — the repayment plan signed, spread per the cap's protection: the firm's error does not license the worker's hardship; the recovery of the firm's mistake rides the same percentage cap as every deduction, which sometimes means the firm's error is recovered over months, and that patience is the price of its own mistake), and the write-off path honest where the arithmetic or equity argues it (the small stale overpayment written off by authority — Accounts 4's write-off discipline, payroll edition — beats the pursuit that costs more than it recovers in naira and far more in trust).

The adjustment's visibility. The layer's slip discipline, closing the chapter: every correction VISIBLE as what it is (the arrears line labelled with its nature and periods, the recovery line with its reference and balance — module 4's anatomy receiving the corrections layer), never smuggled (the correction folded silently into a component's amount is the version drift this track buried — the slip that quietly differs from its structure is unexplainable by design, and unexplainable is the one thing this track's slips are never allowed to be). The corrections layer run this way completes module 3's promise: the frozen run and the honest correction are one system — March means March forever, AND every error March contained has a dated, derived, visible repair. That pairing is what 'corrections travel forward' means, and it is the only version of payroll integrity that survives contact with real months.

lessons.title: Chapter 6 — Staff lending: loans & advances, the mechanics
lessons.html:
Module 4 papered the consent; this chapter builds the machine: the staff lending layer — the policy, the instruments, the flows, and the book. The lending chapter.

The policy. Lending exists as POLICY before the first request (the favour disease's final habitat, fenced in advance): ELIGIBILITY (who may borrow — the confirmation gate, the tenure threshold: the probationer's loan is a risk the policy prices deliberately or declines), LIMITS (the ceiling as a multiple of salary — the affordability logic stated: the loan the recovery cap cannot service inside a reasonable schedule is declined by arithmetic, not by mood), the SCHEDULE conventions (the standard tenors, the recovery rate defaults — inside module 4's percentage cap always), the INTEREST position (interest-free as welfare or priced per policy — a decision with tax and fairness dimensions the adviser and accountant weigh once; whichever is chosen applies evenly), and the APPROVAL route (the requests through the standing flow to the named authority — the founder's personal favour book retired into a policy the payroll seat can administer without courage).

The two instruments. The distinction the layer runs on: the salary advance (THIS month's pay, early — bounded by the earned-to-date logic, recovered in FULL from the next run: the short bridge, governed lightly — the request, the approval, the off-cycle disbursement where urgency demands it, the single recovery; the advance's discipline is its brevity, and the advance that rolls month to month is not an advance but an undocumented loan wearing one — converted formally or closed) and the staff loan (the multi-month instrument — module 4's full consent layer: the agreement with amount, schedule, recovery rate, early-settlement terms, and the separation clause; the DISBURSEMENT through the payment separations like any money movement; the RECOVERY as the governed component advancing per schedule, its balance on every slip; the settlement ceremony at the end). The flows differ; the governance constant: instrument, then announcement, then slip.

The ledger's mirror. The lending layer's accounting, walked once: the disbursement creating the RECEIVABLE (the staff-loan asset account — the firm's money, out, per person: Accounts 4's receivable discipline with employees as the counterparty), the recoveries reducing it run by run (the payroll journal's recovery credits landing against the receivable — module 3's posting anatomy extended one address), the BOOK reconciling monthly (the per-person balances against the slips' balance lines against the ledger's account — three views, one truth, agreeing by construction because they share one parent), and the aged read applying (the loan whose recoveries stalled — the leaver's unsettled balance, the paused schedule — surfaced by the same aging discipline every receivable gets).

The book read. The layer's altitude view, closing the chapter: the lending book read quarterly — the EXPOSURE total (the firm's capital in staff loans, sized against policy's comfort: the book that grows past its ceiling is treasury drift wearing welfare), the DISTRIBUTION (the concentration read — the book that is mostly two names is a different risk than the book that is thin and wide), and the pattern the consultant teaches the owner to read with care: the CHRONIC borrower — the advance every month, the loan atop the loan — is a WELFARE SIGNAL before it is a credit risk (the salary that never reaches month's end has a story: the wage question, the family shock, the debt spiral — the HR track's check-in conversation triggered by payroll's pattern, handled with the dignity the HR track taught), because the lending layer, read humanely, is one of the firm's few honest windows into its people's financial weather — and the firm that notices early helps early, which is both the right thing and the cheaper thing, in that order.

lessons.title: Chapter 7 — Off-cycle payments: outside the ritual, inside governance
lessons.html:
The monthly ritual is the rule; this chapter governs the exceptions — the payments that must move OUTSIDE the run without moving outside governance. The off-cycle chapter.

When off-cycle is legitimate. The catalogue, closed: the MISSED payment (the bounced credit's re-payment — module 3's resolution flow already runs this), the URGENT advance (Chapter 6's bridge, where the payday is too far), the EXIT settlement that cannot wait for the run (module 7's terrain — the final entitlements where timing or terms demand independence), the ERROR whose correction genuinely cannot ride the next run (rare, and the rarity is the point: the arrears layer of Chapter 5 exists precisely so most corrections CAN wait honestly — the off-cycle correction is for the missed-salary class of error, not the missed-allowance class), and the SCHEDULED second runs (the thirteenth month, the festive payout — the planned off-cycles that are really additional ritual runs on the calendar). Everything else waits — and the waiting is defensible because the arrears machinery makes it whole.

The off-cycle as a mini-run. The governance rule: the off-cycle payment runs the SAME ritual at small scale — the document (the additional-pay entry or settlement with its authority), the computation (from the machinery, not a typed net — the off-cycle that hand-computes a net has bypassed the statutory layer, and module 2's projection meets it as an error in the annual true-up), the SEPARATED HANDS (the preparer-approver-releaser separation does not shrink because the amount did — the off-cycle is fraud's preferred vehicle precisely because it travels alone, outside the month's variance read: the single payment with unified hands is the exact shape of the invented one-off), the POSTING (to the same addresses, dated its date), and the SLIP treatment (the off-cycle payment slipped or statement-ed per its nature — the mid-month advance appearing on the month's slip as its recovery's twin, the exit settlement carrying module 7's full statement: nothing moves money to a person without a document the person can read).

The scheduled second run. The legitimate off-cycle at its largest: the thirteenth-month or festive run — planned as a RUN (the calendar's known date, the population defined by the policy, the computation from the rule — the month's-basic or the stated formula, taxed per module 2's treatment of the payment in its month), budgeted from January (the accrual conversation with the accountant — Accounts 4's provision logic: the December obligation built monthly is a line; discovered in November it is a crisis), and communicated per module 4 (the announcement with the arithmetic — the festive payment's net effect shown, because the thirteenth month's PAYE interaction is the season's guaranteed query, pre-answered).

The off-cycle read. The layer's health metric, closing the chapter: the off-cycle COUNT read quarterly — the near-zero count is the ritual working (the calendar absorbing the firm's real payment needs; the exceptions rare and each explained), while the CLIMBING count is a diagnosis (the frequent missed-payment off-cycles indict the bank-detail hygiene or the funding discipline; the frequent urgent advances indict the payday's position against the month's shape or the workforce's financial weather — Chapter 6's welfare read arriving by another door; the frequent 'couldn't wait' corrections indict the run's own quality gates), and the consultant's framing for the owner completes the module's arc: the off-cycle layer is the ritual's exception log, and a ritual whose exceptions are rare, documented, and boring is a ritual that has actually won — which is the standard this track set in module 3 and holds to the end.

lessons.title: Chapter 8 — Case study: HealthTrade's variable year
lessons.html:
The variable layer, governed through a full year. Every chapter clocks in.

Overtime settles (Ch. 2). The one-channel rule holds from module 3's fix; the policy lands beside it: eligibility by role (the counter, warehouse, and driver roles in; the salaried supervisors out — stated in the contracts at the next renewal cycle), the rate convention published, approvals in advance as the norm. The read earns its keep in month three: the Ibadan warehouse's chronic overtime — the same two names, every month — is walked as a staffing gap, not a padding case (the capture trail clean, the approvals honest, the hours real): the roster conversation adds a part-time Saturday hire, and the overtime line falls by 60% — we were paying time-and-a-half for a vacancy, the MD's note reads, which is Chapter 2's price-signal lesson verbatim.

Bonuses & the thirteenth month (Ch. 3, 7). The spot-bonus machinery (module 1's generator case) gets its policy: two named approvers, a per-instance cap, the document with its reason — eleven spot bonuses in the year, each a labelled slip line. The festive payment is formalised the other way: the December payment the firm had made 'when the year allowed' for six years running is recognised for what it had become — the accidental entitlement — and the MD chooses deliberately: the thirteenth month enters policy (stated terms, defined population), the accrual line starts in JANUARY (the accountant's provision building monthly — the first December that isn't a surprise to our own books), and the scheduled second run executes on its announced date with the net-effect announcement pre-answering the PAYE question at the branches.

The commission quarter (Ch. 4). The two salespeople move onto a written scheme: collection-based (the receivables discipline arguing for money over paper — the Selling track's logic applied), tiered, quarterly, with the clawback clause stated and signed. The computation generates from the collection register — the first quarter's statements land beside the payout slips (each seller's source list, tier, and total — one seller finds a missing collection in her own statement's list; the correction runs forward and the channel's credibility is purchased exactly as module 4 taught). The clause earns its keep in quarter two: a ₦480,000 collection bounces after the payout — the reversal nets against the running quarter per the clause, visible in the statement's lines, and the conversation is arithmetic, not argument: the rule we signed is the rule that ran.

Corrections & lending (Ch. 5-6). The review cycle's one late conclusion becomes the backdated-increment case: effective March, processed May — the machinery derives the two months' delta per period, the arrears line lands with its breakdown, the announcement carries the arithmetic. One overpayment surfaces (a proration miss on a mid-month joiner — the firm's error): the conversation first, the arithmetic walked, the recovery consented over four months inside the cap — your mistake, my schedule, the employee notes, accurately, and the file agrees. The lending book's first year: policy adopted (confirmation gate, salary-multiple ceiling, interest-free by choice, even by rule), five loans and nine advances administered through the flow, the book reconciling three-ways monthly — and one chronic-advance pattern (the same till operator, four consecutive months) handled as Chapter 6 taught: the welfare conversation before the credit decision, surfacing a family medical situation — the response a governed hardship loan and the HR track's support conversation, the pattern read as a signal, not a nuisance. The year's off-cycle count: six — four bounced-credit re-payments, one urgent advance, one exit settlement — each documented, each boring. The MD's closing note: the one-offs used to be where the system ended; now they are just the part of it that moves.

lessons.title: Chapter 9 — Common mistakes & the fifth law
lessons.html:
The variable layer's scar tissue. Symptom → disease → fix.

Pattern 1 — the cash envelope. Symptom: bonuses beside the bank run; generosity the ledger never saw; the tax the projection never computed. Disease: the off-book variable layer (Ch. 1, 3) — a parallel economy with every disease at once. Fix: every bonus a document through the machinery — labelled on the slip, posted to its address, taxed in its month — generosity kept AND governed.

Pattern 2 — commission from memory. Symptom: the month-end notebook negotiation; the firm's biggest incentive re-litigated monthly; the star seller's version always larger. Disease: the scheme unwritten and the computation sourceless (Ch. 4). Fix: the written scheme, the computation from selling documents, the statement as the seller's own reconciliation — one configuration, zero arguments.

Pattern 3 — the overtime leak. Symptom: chronic hours nobody questions; the padding nobody can disprove; time-and-a-half as a standing budget line. Disease: no policy, side channels, after-the-fact approval (Ch. 2). Fix: the role-based policy, the one channel from the capture layer, approval before hours, and the monthly read — overtime as a price signal, answered with staffing.

Pattern 4 — the clawback surprise. Symptom: the recovery discovered on a slip after a big return; the confiscation grievance; the scheme's downside improvised in anger. Disease: the reversal unclause-d (Ch. 4) and the never-surprised law breached (Ch. 5). Fix: the clawback designed in daylight, stated in the signed scheme, netted visibly — and every recovery, of any kind, conversationed before deducted.

Pattern 5 — the rolling advance. Symptom: the advance every month, silently renewed; the undocumented loan wearing a bridge's name; the chronic borrower unnoticed. Disease: the instruments confused and the pattern unread (Ch. 6). Fix: the advance recovered in full next run or converted formally; the book read quarterly; the chronic pattern met as a welfare signal first — noticed early, helped early.

Pattern 6 — the off-cycle as normal. Symptom: payments moving whenever, computed by hand, released by whoever; the month's story scattered across ad-hoc transfers. Disease: the exception become the method (Ch. 7) — fraud's preferred vehicle normalised. Fix: the legitimate catalogue closed, the mini-run governance (document, machinery computation, separated hands, posting, statement), and the off-cycle count read as the ritual's health metric.

The fifth law. The structure computes, the state rides, the run seals, the account renders — and now the one-offs join: variable pay is governed, not improvised — every overtime hour through one channel, every bonus a labelled document, every commission computed from source with its statement, every correction derived and travelling forward, every loan an instrument with a visible balance, and every off-cycle a mini-run with the same hands and the same paper. The variable layer is where structure leaks or where it proves itself — and the firm whose one-offs are documents has a payroll that flexes without leaking, which is the whole difference between generosity and chaos. Module 6 climbs to the layer that changes the fixed pay itself: increments, reviews, and the governance of the pay structure over time.

pay_reviews.title: Payroll 6 — Increments, Reviews & Pay Governance
pay_reviews.desc: How pay changes: the annual cycle with the envelope set first, the increment matrix pricing calibrated evidence, band maintenance against market, inflation, and the minimum wage, promotion re-pricing with the compression and equity reads, the payroll budget as the owner's instrument, and the no-quiet-raises perimeter.

lessons.title: Chapter 1 — Reviews on structure and evidence
lessons.html:
Modules 1-5 governed pay as it IS; this module governs how it CHANGES — the review cycle that moves the fixed pay itself — and its thesis is the sixth law forming: pay reviews run on structure and evidence, not on squeak and mood.

Why pay must be reviewed at all. The Nigerian reality stated first, because it drives everything: unreviewed nominal pay DECAYS — inflation erodes real pay silently, month by month, so the firm that 'kept salaries stable' for three years has in truth cut everyone's real pay substantially without a single decision (the decay is a pay cut nobody announced, and the workforce experiences it exactly as one: the HR track's attrition referendum reads it back as the year-two exodus, the side-hustle drift, and the counter-offer season) — which converts the review from a generosity question into a MAINTENANCE question: the review cycle is how a firm keeps the pay bargain's real value deliberate instead of letting arithmetic quietly break it. The second driver beside it: EVIDENCE accumulates — the HR track's performance machinery produces calibrated, documented ratings annually, and evidence that changes nothing teaches everyone that the folder was theatre (HR 5's ambush law has a payroll corollary: the appraisal that never touches pay eventually never touches effort).

The two inputs. Every review cycle reconciles exactly two forces, and naming them keeps the cycle honest: the FIRM'S CAPACITY (what the budget can carry — Chapter 6's envelope, set from the numbers before the cycle opens, because the affordability decided after seeing the wish-list is a negotiation, while the envelope decided before is a constraint everyone shares) and the PERSON'S EVIDENCE (the calibrated rating, the band position, the certified growth — the HR track's outputs, consumed as the cycle's raw material). The cycle's machinery — the matrix (Chapter 3), the bands (Chapter 4), the governance (Chapter 7) — exists to reconcile these two inputs EVENLY: same evidence, same treatment, inside the same envelope.

One cycle, not rolling favours. The structural decision that shapes everything: pay changes happen at the CYCLE (the annual review, on the calendar, all at once) plus the defined movement events (the promotion, the confirmation step where policy grants one — HR 7's documents), and NOT as a rolling stream of individual renegotiations — because the rolling model is the favour system with a calendar problem (the raise granted to whoever asked loudest, whenever they asked — module 1's negotiated-from-memory disease applied to changes; the quiet raise that module 7's governance will formally outlaw), while the cycle model concentrates the firm's one hardest conversation into one season with one process, one envelope, and one announcement — which is cheaper in management attention, fairer by construction, and defensible forever. The module's map follows the cycle's own arc: the calendar event (2), the matrix (3), the bands beneath (4), the promotions and equity reads (5), the budget above (6), the governance and letters around (7) — and HealthTrade's first cycle run end to end (8).

lessons.title: Chapter 2 — The review cycle: the calendar event
lessons.html:
The cycle as machinery: its stages, in order, each feeding the next — the run's ritual discipline applied to the year's biggest pay event. The cycle chapter.

The stages. The sequence, walked: 1 — the envelope set (Chapter 6's budget work concluding BEFORE the cycle opens: the total increment pool as a number the owner has already accepted — the cycle that opens without an envelope closes as an argument); 2 — the evidence in (the HR track's appraisal season concluding first by design — the calibrated ratings landing as the cycle's input file: the two calendars sequenced deliberately, appraisals then reviews, because ratings finalised DURING pay season are ratings written backwards from desired raises — the calibration integrity of HR 5 protected by the calendar itself); 3 — the matrix applied (Chapter 3 — the ratings and band positions converted to proposed increments, mechanically, as the STARTING grid); 4 — the adjustments within governance (the below-band priorities, the retention flags, the equity corrections — Chapter 5's reads applied as deliberate exceptions with written reasons, inside the envelope: the matrix proposes, humans decide, the envelope constrains); 5 — the approval (the full grid — every name, current, proposed, new band position, cost — approved by the authority in one sitting: the review's version of module 3's names-reading approval); 6 — the letters (Chapter 7 — individual, with effective dates and net effects); 7 — the execution (the assignments updated by the event, effective-dated — module 1's machinery; the structures re-versioned where Chapter 4 moved bands); and 8 — the run (the first affected run carrying the changes, its variance read pre-loaded with the cycle's grid as the expected-changes list — module 3's review consuming module 6's output: the machinery meshing).

The timing. The cycle placed deliberately: aligned to the fiscal year and the appraisal season (the evidence fresh, the budget known), at the same time EVERY year (the workforce that knows review season builds expectations to it — the fixed payday's logic at annual scale: the cycle that drifts teaches that pay changes are weather), and with its effective date clean (the year's start or a fixed month — the mid-month effective date buying proration complexity for no benefit).

The cycle's size honesty. The eleven-person reality, stated as every track states it: HealthTrade's cycle is the founder, the accountant, and the payroll seat, one afternoon of grid work and a week of letters — the SHAPE, small (the envelope a paragraph, the calibration a conversation, the approval a sitting) — and the discipline is not the paperwork's weight but the sequence's integrity: envelope before wishes, evidence before numbers, grid before letters, letters before slips. The firm that keeps the sequence at eleven people scales it to a hundred without redesign — which is the academy's standing promise, kept here at the layer where growing firms break most publicly (the fifty-person firm still doing rolling favours is the one whose pay chaos makes the trade's gossip).

lessons.title: Chapter 3 — The increment matrix: evidence into naira
lessons.html:
The cycle's computational heart: the INCREMENT MATRIX — the published logic that converts a rating and a band position into a proposed increment. The matrix chapter.

The matrix's shape. Two axes, one output: the RATING (the HR track's calibrated outcome — the honest scale of HR 5, with 'meets' as its honourable centre) crossed with the POSITION IN BAND (where the person's pay sits inside their grade's range — the compa-ratio concept taught practically: below the band's midpoint, at it, above it), yielding the increment percentage per cell — with the matrix's internal logic taught so consultants can design one, not just admire one: the HIGH-rating-LOW-position cell carries the largest increments (the strong performer paid under their band is the firm's biggest fairness debt and flight risk at once — the matrix pays the debt fastest), the MEETS-at-midpoint cell carries the maintenance increment (the real-pay-decay repair of Chapter 1 — the cost-of-living reality answered for the solid performer), the HIGH-position cells taper (the person at band top has outgrown the band — the answer is Chapter 5's promotion question or Chapter 4's band question, not an increment that breaches the band's own meaning), and the LOW-rating cells carry small-to-zero (with the capability process of HR 5 owning the person, not the matrix — the review is not the performance conversation; it consumes its output).

Why a matrix at all. The argument, made once for every owner who calls it rigid: EVENNESS (same rating, same position, same increment — the favour system structurally displaced: the matrix cannot like anyone), BUDGET CONTROL (the matrix's cells priced against the population BEFORE approval — the envelope test run on the grid, the cells tuned until the total fits: the affordability engineered, not discovered), DEFENSIBILITY (the increment explained by pointing — the rating, the position, the cell: module 4's answered-by-pointing reaching the year's most sensitive question), and SPEED (the cycle's grid generated in minutes, reviewed in an afternoon — the rolling-negotiation year compressed into a sitting). The matrix's honest limits stated beside it: it PROPOSES — Chapter 2's stage 4 lets governance adjust with written reasons — and its calibration is only as good as the ratings feeding it (the leniency-inflated ratings of an uncalibrated appraisal season turn the matrix into an expensive rubber stamp: HR 5's calibration is this chapter's load-bearing dependency, and the two-track consultant sells them as the pair they are).

The below-band priority. The matrix's first exception rule, promoted to policy: the person BELOW their band's floor is corrected FIRST, before the matrix runs — the correction to the band minimum is not an increment (not a reward, not a rating outcome); it is the structure enforcing its own promise (module 1's band architecture made a floor; the floor means something or nothing), funded ahead of the envelope's discretionary pool, and communicated as what it is (the correction letter distinct from the increment letter — the person told the band is real, which lands as the structure's justice exactly as HealthTrade's module 1 case landed). The chapter's closing frame: the matrix is the evenness law given a calculator — and the firm that publishes its logic (the axes and the philosophy, not the cell values' gossip) has told the workforce the one thing that defuses review season: the path to more money is evidence and growth, and the path is the same for everyone.

lessons.title: Chapter 4 — Band maintenance: the structure against the market
lessons.html:
Increments move people WITHIN bands; this chapter governs the bands THEMSELVES — the annual maintenance that keeps the structure honest against the market, inflation, and the law. The bands chapter.

The annual band review. The structure's own review, run beside the cycle: each grade's band tested against three forces — the MARKET (what the trade pays for the role now: the labour-market read of HR 2, refreshed — the band that lags the market is the recruitment funnel's silent saboteur and the exit interview's recurring line; the read's sources practical: the firm's own hiring data (the offers declined and the asks that declined them), the trade's networks, the adviser's and peers' soundings), INFLATION (the real-value check of Chapter 1 applied to the band itself — the band unmoved for three years has drifted down the market by arithmetic alone), and the LAW (the national minimum wage as the absolute floor — the statutory minimum the adviser confirms current, against which the LOWEST band's floor is tested every year without exception: the minimum wage change is a compliance event, not a negotiation, and the reform era's movements make this an annual confirmation, not an assumption — the band floor below the legal floor is a violation wearing a structure).

The band move's machinery. When the review moves a band: the structure RE-VERSIONED (module 1's amendment discipline — the new band effective-dated, the old preserved), the move's two distinct effects handled separately: the FLOOR effect (everyone below the new floor corrected to it — Chapter 3's below-band rule firing automatically at the band's own move) and the POSITION effect (everyone else's band position recalculated — the person at midpoint now below it, which feeds NEXT cycle's matrix rather than triggering immediate increments: the band move and the increment cycle are separate instruments, and conflating them double-spends the envelope), and the move COSTED before approval (the floor corrections' total is the band move's price tag — presented with the move, decided with open eyes).

Cost-of-living versus merit. The distinction that keeps both honest, taught for the announcement as much as the arithmetic: the COLA-type adjustment (the across-the-board response to inflation — everyone's real pay maintained: applied as a band move plus a uniform component where the firm runs one, communicated as maintenance — this is not a raise; this is your pay keeping its meaning) versus the MERIT increment (the matrix's differentiated output — communicated as earned), because the firm that blends them into one number teaches that merit is automatic (the strong performer who got 12% learns 8% of it was inflation and feels the 4%), while the firm that names them separately gets credit for both — the maintenance honoured as fairness, the merit honoured as recognition: one letter, two lines, twice the trust.

The frozen-band autopsy. The chapter's cautionary pattern, told for every prospect conversation: the firm whose bands froze for five years — real pay down by half, the market moved on, the recruitment funnel dried (the offers laughed at), the tenured staff trapped-then-gone in a wave (the exit interviews unanimous), and the panicked correction costing in one year what maintenance would have cost in five, plus the rebuilding — the arithmetic the consultant shows with the client's own inflation history, because the frozen band FEELS free (no decision, no cost, no letter) and is the most expensive pay decision a firm makes by not making it. The chapter's law-fragment: the structure is only as honest as its maintenance — bands reviewed annually, moved deliberately, floored legally, and separated cleanly from merit.

lessons.title: Chapter 5 — Promotion re-pricing & the equity reads
lessons.html:
The individual movements the cycle prices, and the population-level fairness reads that keep the whole structure honest. The equity chapter.

Promotion re-pricing. HR 7's promotion event, receiving its pay discipline: the promoted person is priced INTO THE NEW BAND (the placement conversation — typically at or near the new band's floor-to-lower-third depending on readiness, per the firm's stated convention), NOT given a percentage on old pay — because the percent-on-old-pay promotion manufactures the trade's commonest inequity by arithmetic: the promoted-from-below person lands under the band (or under peers hired directly into the grade), doing the bigger job at the smaller pay, with the gap visible to everyone the moment module 4's band transparency exists (the promotion that nets a person less than an external hire for the same seat is the structure contradicting itself in public). The discipline's edge cases handled by rule: the promotion whose new-band placement exceeds the matrix-era increments is CORRECT (the promotion is a re-pricing event, not an increment — budgeted in Chapter 6's headcount plan, not the increment envelope), and the small-step promotion into an overlapping band placed thoughtfully (the overlap zone is where the placement convention earns its keep).

The compression read. The first population scan, run annually beside the cycle: COMPRESSION — the gap between adjacent layers shrinking until it inverts (the new hire priced at today's market landing above the three-year incumbent whose increments lagged; the supervisor earning barely above the supervised — the differential that made the rung worth climbing, eroded): read by listing each grade's population against the one below (the overlaps flagged, the inversions treated as urgent — the incumbent who discovers the newcomer's premium is a resignation letter in draft, and module 4's confidentiality only delays the discovery), and repaired deliberately (the lagging incumbents' corrections prioritised in the envelope — the compression repair as a named budget line, because compression is the market's message that the internal maintenance fell behind the external reality, and the repair bill is the lag's invoice).

The equity scan. The harder read, run with the care it demands: pay equity across the population — like work compared with like pay (within grade, controlling for band position and tenure: the scan asking whether any PATTERN — gender being the scan's classic and legally live axis, but tenure cohorts and hire-era effects equally — explains pay differences that evidence does not), read at altitude first (the grade-level averages and distributions — the HR track's numbers-are-questions epistemics governing absolutely: the pattern surfaced is a question for investigation, not a verdict for announcement), investigated by cases (the flagged pairs walked against their documents — the offer history, the increment trail, the red-circles: sometimes the difference has a documented story; sometimes it has none, and the none is the finding), and REPAIRED where found (the correction through the cycle's machinery, communicated per module 4's individual-change discipline — and the adviser engaged where the finding has legal weight, per the standing grammar). The scan's annual habit is the point: the firm that reads its own equity yearly repairs drifts of months; the firm that never reads repairs decades, publicly, under counsel.

The red-circle clock. The legacy arrangements of module 1, managed over time: the red-circled pay (above-band, personal-to-holder) held FLAT through cycles (the band rises toward it — the increment matrix's high-position taper doing its designed work; the red circle is not punished, merely not compounded) until the band catches up and the circle dissolves (the arrangement re-absorbed into structure — the event noted, the history closed), with the discipline being patience-by-design: the red circle inherited from the pre-structure era is a debt the structure retires by growth, not by confrontation — the module's quietest lesson in how architecture fixes what arguments cannot.

lessons.title: Chapter 6 — The payroll budget: the owner's instrument
lessons.html:
The cycle's ceiling and the owner's steering wheel: the PAYROLL BUDGET — the layer where pay meets the business's arithmetic. The budget chapter.

Payroll cost in the business's shape. The framing numbers, taught for the owner conversation: TOTAL payroll cost (module 1's third number, summed — gross plus employer statutory plus the variable layer's run-rate: the employer-cost model at population scale) read against the business (as a share of revenue and of gross margin — the trade's ratios varying by vertical: the distribution business and the pharmacy carry different payroll shapes, and the consultant benchmarks against the firm's own trend first, the vertical's norms second), TRENDED (the ratio's drift telling the structural story — payroll growing faster than gross margin is a trajectory conversation, not a crisis, when read early), and DECOMPOSED (the cost by branch and function via Accounts 6's dimensions — the payroll journal's cost-center addresses making the question 'where does our payroll go?' a report, not a research project: the trilogy's machinery answering the owner's biggest cost question from its ordinary operation).

The envelope. The cycle's budget discipline, mechanised: the increment ENVELOPE set before the cycle (Chapter 2's stage one) from the business's numbers — the affordability modeled (the envelope's percentage against the year's plan: what the P&L carries, what the cash carries — the accountant's session, with Accounts 7's statements as the evidence), the envelope's COMPOSITION named (the maintenance share for the COLA reality, the merit pool for the matrix, the named repair lines — the below-band corrections, the compression repairs of Chapter 5 — each sized: the envelope with named compartments survives the cycle; the single number gets eaten by whoever moves first), and the envelope's honesty defended in both directions (the envelope too small for maintenance is Chapter 4's frozen-band autopsy on the instalment plan — the owner shown the real-pay arithmetic and the attrition bill before choosing it; the envelope inflated past the business's arithmetic is next year's retrenchment conversation prepaid — the sustainable raise beats the impressive one, and the workforce, told honestly, knows it).

The what-if machinery. Module 1's modeling discipline at cycle scale: the review modeled before it is offered — the grid's scenarios costed (matrix tuning A versus B, the band move's price tag, the promotion slate's total — each scenario's monthly and annual cost, employer-statutory included, because the increment's true cost is the third number's delta, not the gross delta), the headcount plan integrated (HR 2's staffing frame — the planned hires' full cost in the same model: the year's people budget as ONE picture, increments and hires together, against one affordability), and the model's output being the owner's decision-grade page: this envelope, these bands, this slate — costing this, monthly, from these dates. The affordability conversation done this way is the module's quiet gift to the founder: the year's hardest numbers, decided once, with evidence, in daylight — instead of relitigated at every request, from memory, in corridors.

The budget's year. The instrument's rhythm, closing the chapter: the budget set annually with the envelope, TRACKED monthly (the run's totals against the plan — module 3's approval already reads this; the budget line makes the reading cumulative), and VARIANCE-read quarterly (the drift explained: the overtime trend of module 5's read, the unplanned hires, the off-cycle creep — each a named cause, because the payroll budget that drifts silently is the business's largest cost unmanaged, and the one this trilogy exists to make boring).

lessons.title: Chapter 7 — Governing the cycle: authorities, letters & the no-quiet-raises law
lessons.html:
The cycle's governance shell: who decides, how it is communicated, and the law that keeps every pay change inside the machinery. The governance chapter.

The authorities. The cycle's separated powers, in the academy's pattern: the MATRIX and bands are configuration (the narrowest pen — changed at the cycle by the design conversation, versioned), the GRID is proposed by the machinery and adjusted by management within governance (the written-reason discipline for every deviation from the matrix's proposal — the adjustment without a reason is the favour system re-entering through the exception door), the APPROVAL is the named authority's in one sitting (the whole grid, every name — the founder at HealthTrade's scale; the committee where scale demands: module 3's real-approval standard at the year's biggest pay moment), and the EXECUTION is the payroll seat's through the standing machinery (the assignments by event, the letters from the grid — the deciders and the executors distinct, as every track requires). Nobody adjusts their own row: the cycle's participants with pay in the grid — the payroll seat, the managers — have their rows decided by their principals (HR 6's nobody-files-their-own-case law, at the pay table).

The letters. The cycle's communication, per module 4's laws: INDIVIDUAL letters (the pay change is personal — the letter with the current, the new, the effective date, and the NET effect per module 1's modeling: the ₦20k gross that yields ₦14k net, shown, because the un-shown net difference is payday's guaranteed query), the maintenance and merit named separately (Chapter 4's two lines), the below-band and compression corrections named as corrections (the structure's justice, claimed), the letters BEFORE the first affected run with the week's runway (never-surprised-by-payday at the year's biggest change), and filed to the record (HR 7's event discipline — the letter is the assignment's authorising document). The population announcement beside them: the cycle's completion announced with its process honoured (the matrix's logic, the bands' review, the envelope's reality — the HOW public per module 4's transparency line, the WHOs private forever).

The no-quiet-raises law. The cycle's perimeter, stated absolutely: every change to fixed pay travels through the CYCLE or a defined MOVEMENT EVENT — no third path (the quiet raise granted mid-year outside both is module 1's quiet edit wearing a kindness: invisible to the envelope, corrosive to the evenness, and discoverable by exactly the person it will wound most), with the mid-cycle EXCEPTION governed rather than denied: the genuine market correction (the critical role's band suddenly wrong — the band question handled as Chapter 4's machinery, off-cycle but on-process) and the counter-offer case (HR 6's honest framing applied: where the firm chooses to counter, the counter travels as a documented exception with its written reason, its approval, and its letter — rare by design, because Chapter's machinery makes the systematic version unnecessary: the firm whose bands are maintained and whose matrix pays evidence has removed the resignation-as-negotiation channel's fuel). The law's enforcement is structural, as always: the assignment writable only by its owning events (module 1's fence), the cycle and the movement events being the only events that own it — the quiet raise not forbidden but IMPOSSIBLE, which is this academy's preferred kind of rule.

lessons.title: Chapter 8 — Case study: HealthTrade's first review cycle
lessons.html:
The cycle, run end to end in its first year on structure. Every chapter clocks in.

The envelope and the evidence (Ch. 2, 6). The sequence holds from the start: the accountant's affordability session lands the envelope in November (the year's numbers carrying a defined pool — compartments named: maintenance share, merit pool, and two repair lines pre-sized), the appraisal season concludes first (HR 5's calibrated ratings in — the calendar sequenced deliberately, and the one manager who tries to 'revisit' a rating during pay season is declined by the calendar itself: ratings closed in October; we are pricing them, not rewriting them). The band review runs beside it: the market read from the year's own hiring data (two declined offers at the counter-role band's floor — the market's message, received), the minimum-wage confirmation with the adviser (the lowest band's floor cleared with margin), and ONE band moved — the counter roles' band lifted, its floor corrections costed as the move's price tag and approved with open eyes.

The matrix and the grid (Ch. 3, 5). The matrix designed in one sitting (three ratings by three band positions — nine cells, the philosophy walked: debt-paying cell largest, meets-at-midpoint as maintenance, high-position tapered), the grid generated in minutes — and the adjustments arrive as governance, not favours: TWO below-band corrections fire first (the band move's floor effect — the corrections funded from their named line, the letters drafted as corrections: the structure's justice, second edition), ONE compression flag (a three-year till operator overlapped by the year's new hire — the incumbent's repair prioritised with its written reason: market moved; her increments lagged; the gap is ours, not hers), and one promotion priced properly (the Ibadan senior storekeeper of HR 8's succession — placed into the new band's lower third, NOT percent-on-old: the placement exceeding any matrix cell, correctly, as a re-pricing event from the headcount plan's budget). The equity scan's first run reads clean at grade level with one flagged pair — walked against documents, the difference explained by a documented red-circle — the scan filed with its finding: clean, one explained, repeat annually.

The letters and the run (Ch. 7, 2). The founder approves the grid in one sitting — every name, every current-and-new, the envelope's total confirmed against the pool (first year I've seen the whole picture on one page). The letters go out with the week's runway: maintenance and merit as two lines (the branch reaction validating Chapter 4's design — the maintenance line landing as respect: they named the inflation instead of pretending it was a raise), net effects shown, the corrections named as corrections. The population announcement honours the process at the branch meetings. The first affected run's variance read is pre-loaded with the grid as its expected list — module 3's review consuming module 6's output, every variance matched, the run sealing clean on schedule.

The perimeter tested (Ch. 7). The year delivers its test in month eight: a Lagos pharmacist resigns with a competitor's offer; the MD wants to counter. The machinery answers instead of the mood: the band checked first (current — the market read four months old and holding), the person's grid position reviewed (paid at band, rated honestly), and the honest conversation held per HR 6's framing — the firm counters ONCE, as a documented exception with its written reason and letter (the specialist licence's replacement cost pricing the exception), and the file notes the systemic answer beside the individual one: if this recurs, it is a band question, not a counter-offer policy. The pharmacist stays; the exception stays rare; the perimeter holds. The MD's cycle note closes the case: pay used to be twenty-seven separate arguments spread across a year; now it is one season, one grid, one envelope — and the arguments stopped because the answers moved into the structure.

lessons.title: Chapter 9 — Common mistakes & the sixth law
lessons.html:
The review layer's scar tissue. Symptom → disease → fix.

Pattern 1 — the squeaky-wheel raise. Symptom: raises to whoever asks loudest, whenever; the quiet diligent underpaid for their silence; resignation as the only reliable negotiation channel. Disease: rolling favours instead of a cycle (Ch. 1-2). Fix: one cycle on the calendar, the matrix pricing evidence, the perimeter law — the path to more money the same for everyone.

Pattern 2 — the frozen band. Symptom: 'stable' salaries through years of inflation; offers laughed at; the tenured wave-exit; the panic correction costing five years' maintenance at once. Disease: real-pay decay unmanaged (Ch. 1, 4) — the most expensive decision made by not making it. Fix: the annual band review against market, inflation, and the minimum wage; maintenance named and funded; the decay arithmetic shown to the owner yearly.

Pattern 3 — the percent-on-old-pay promotion. Symptom: the promoted earning under the band and under external peers; the bigger job at the smaller pay; the structure contradicting itself in public. Disease: the promotion treated as an increment instead of a re-pricing (Ch. 5). Fix: placement into the new band by convention, budgeted from the headcount plan — the rung worth climbing because the price honours it.

Pattern 4 — compression ignored. Symptom: new hires above incumbents; supervisors barely above supervised; the discovery followed by the resignation. Disease: the market repriced the entrance while the inside lagged (Ch. 5). Fix: the annual compression read, the inversions urgent, the repairs a named envelope line — the lag's invoice paid deliberately, not at exit interviews.

Pattern 5 — the unbudgeted cycle. Symptom: increments decided then discovered unaffordable; the envelope negotiated after the wish-list; next year's retrenchment prepaying this year's generosity. Disease: capacity consulted last (Ch. 6). Fix: the envelope before the cycle, compartments named, scenarios costed at the third number — the sustainable raise beating the impressive one.

Pattern 6 — the quiet raise. Symptom: pay changes outside any cycle or event; the grid that doesn't match the assignments; the favour discovered by exactly whom it wounds. Disease: the third path left open (Ch. 7). Fix: the assignment writable only by its owning events — the cycle and the movements — with the governed mid-cycle exception documented and rare: the quiet raise made impossible, not merely forbidden.

The sixth law. The structure computes, the state rides, the run seals, the account renders, the one-offs join — and now the change itself is governed: pay reviews run on structure and evidence — one cycle with its envelope set first, the matrix pricing calibrated evidence evenly, bands maintained against market, inflation, and law, promotions re-priced into their bands, equity read annually, every change lettered with its net, and no path to changed pay outside the machinery. The firm that governs pay's changes as well as its computation has closed the layer's last leak — and module 7 now takes the machinery to its hardest single computation: the exit, where everything this track built must settle one person's whole account, once, correctly, on a deadline.
